title.narrative: Norwegian Peoples Aid (NPA) - Främja ett hållbart samhälle i Irak 2023-2025
Norwegian Peoples Aid (NPA) - Promoting a sustainable society in Iraq 2023-2025

description.narrative:
Insatsen avser att ge stöd till en uppsättning civilsamhälles organisationer som spelar en aktiv roll i arbetet för demokrati, inkludering och lösningar på Iraks miljö- och klimatkris. Programperioden omfattar oktober 2023-juni 2025 och kommer att fokusera på:
- stödja marginaliserade samhällen (kvinnor och ungdomsgrupper-WYGs), att få ökad representation, deltagande och inflytande i beslutsprocesser på alla nivåer och
- stärka civilsamhällets organisationer (CSO) så att de effektivt kan påverka beslut i miljö- och klimatfrågor i Irak.
Insatsens geografiska omfattning berör provinserna Kurdistan, Kirkuk, Diyala, Bagdad, Basra, Dhi Qar, Muthanna, Maysan, Ninewa, AlAnbar, Babil och Salah alDin.
Insatsen är markerad med OECD DAC koden 15150 - demokratiskt deltagande och civilsamhälle eftersom insatsen bidrar till att öka CSOs möjligheter att arbeta för demokrati, inkludering och för att bidra till hållbara lösningar på Iraks miljö- och klimatkris.

The contribution aims to support a set of civil society organisations (CSOs) that are play an active role in working for democracy, inclusion, environmental protection and sustainable development in Iraq. The programme period covers October 2023 - June 2025 and will focus on:
- supporting marginalised communities (women and youth groups-WYGs), to have increased representation, participation and influence in the decision-making processes and
- strengthening Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) so they can effectively influence decisions and promote environment protection in Iraq
The geographic scope of the programme covers: Locations within the provinces of Kurdistan Region, Kirkuk, Diyala, Baghdad, Basra, Dhi Qar, Muthanna, Maysan, Ninewa, Al­Anbar, Babil, and Salah al­Din.
The contribution is coded as OECD DAC code 15150 - Democratic participation and civil society, since the aim of the project is to strengthen civil society organisations ability to play an active role in for democracy, inclusion and environmental protection.

The longterm goal of the programme is to support and empower communities and CSOs in their efforts to promote a democratic, inclusive and environmentally sustainable society in Iraq. The programme will contribute to a more stable and peaceful Iraq by empowering communities through involvement of women and young people from diverse segments of society, and CSOs to take an active role in working for democracy, inclusion, environmental protection and sustainable development. By empowering these actors, peace, stability, sustainability, and inclusive governance are promoted in Iraq.
NPA believes that democratisation is a prerequisite for a more peaceful society and for stability and environmental sustainability. To this end NPA believes it is critical to strengthen civil society and local communities since they are engaged in seeking change. If they are strengthened they can influence the direction of change in a positive manner.
The theory of change include two outcomes: Outcome Challenge 1: The programme intends to see marginalised communities (women and youth groups WYGs), to have increased representation, participation and influence in the decisionmaking processes in Iraq.
Outcome Challenge 2: The programme intends to see strengthened Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) effectively influence decisions and promote environment protection in Iraq.
NPA has several partners that will particularly contribute to outcome 1. They are involved in a number of different areas of work concerning policy development at national, regional and local levels and in services delivery targeting refugees that suffered from violence and genocide during ISIL.
With this in mind the project intends to allow women and youth will play a lead role in making positive change in their communities and to gain better capacity to influence and participate in the decisionmaking process in Iraq. For this to happen NPA partners will empower women, youth and community members through capacity building activities and mobilization in advocacy for their rights and needs to be addressed in decisionmaking at different levels. NPA partners will draw on their connections with women members of political parties in trainings and make use of media to increase visibility and impact of the activities to a wider public. The topics on the agenda in the influencing activities concern for instance laws the need for amendments of the Identity Card Law to allow the children of mothers raped by ISIS members to gain ID cards, amendments to the law antidomestic violence law and the civil service law.

During 2023 and 2024 NPA was planning for a program assumed to be ongoing from 2023 - 2027. During the inception period 2023 - 2024 considerable efforts were directed towards facilitating and enhancing the proposal packages of the local partners. Work was undertaken to refine and redraft these packages, ensuring alignment with the overall objectives and requirements of the programme. This collaborative approach strengthened the quality and coherence of the proposals, fostering a more integrated and synergistic programme framework.
NPA also outlined the steps for conducting a programme baseline. This baseline assessment will serve as a foundational measure, providing valuable insights into the current status and potential areas for improvement within the programme. The findings of this baseline analysis will inform subsequent decision making processes and will contribute to the overall programme strategy.
NPA has identified three potential partners that will actively contribute in the programme. The selection of these partners involved an evaluation process, considering factors such as geographical coverage, expertise, resources, and alignment with programme objectives.
On February 14 2024 NPA with local partners in Iraq and KRG (and IMS with local partners) participated in Sida's workshop on environmental questions in Iraq and in the Middle East. Following the workshop Sida organised discussions on lessons learned at February 14. One learned lesson is that local partners appreciated the possibility to learn relevant facts about the environment in Iraq.
During spring 2024 Sida organised three discussions on lessons learned with NPA, local partners (and IMS with local partners). NPA and IMS with partners asked Sida to do a second "14 February seminar" in autumn 2024. However, in July 2024 the Swedish government decided to phase out all bilateral development cooperation with Iraq. Hence, the agendas were changed.
At the annual meeting in Oslo May 2024 Sida discussed the theory of change used by NPA. NPA works to increase the influence of women and young people in decision making positions, in CSO and in political parties and in municipalities. (See Dox: 23/00081375, 23/00081388)
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
